resolutions.answer: Exactly one probe-exercised behavior is determined differently by joinspec.md than by joiner.py: the ordering of lists with two or more items. joinspec.md clause 'Items appear in the order given in the list' mandates the given-order join; joiner.py computes ', '.join(reversed(items)). This diverges on probes 1, 3, and 5 (spec-determined 'x, y' / 'one, two, three' / 'b, a' vs joiner.py's 'y, x' / 'three, two, one' / 'a, b'). No probe-exercised behavior is left undetermined: every probe is a flat list of plain strings, whose join output is fully characterized by separator, order, and the empty-list case, and joinspec.md fixes all three; separator (probes 1/3/5), singleton rendering (probes 0/4), and empty-list rendering (probe 2) are determined identically to joiner.py. Full per-probe traceability and completeness argument in ea-behavior-statement.md.

The root-executed validate-child / create-child / child-return nodes settle Q2.
